    (k : ℕ+) (f : ℕ → ℂ)
    (hf_mul : ∀ m n, f (m * n) = f m * f n)
    (hf_one : f 1 = 1)
    (hf_range : ∀ n, ∃ j : Fin k, f n = Complex.exp (2 * Real.pi * Complex.I * (j : ℂ) / (k : ℂ)))
    (ω : ℂ) (hω_mem : ∃ n, f n = ω) :
    ∃ x y z : ℕ, x * x + y * y = z * z ∧ f x = ω ∧ f y = ω ∧ f z = ω := by
  sorry
directions.proof_strategy: The ω = 1 case follows from the paper's vanishing-averages/pretentious-function decomposition. For general ω, one might try: (1) construct a modified multiplicative function g related to f and ω whose level set at 1 corresponds to f's level set at ω, then apply the paper's machinery to g — but g(n) = f(n)·ω^{-v(n)} for suitable v is not completely multiplicative; (2) use the dilation structure: if (a,b,c) is a Pythagorean triple with f(a)=f(b)=f(c)=1, then for any prime p with f(p)=ω, the dilated triple (pa,pb,pc) gives f(pa)=ω·f(a)=ω, etc., but this requires f(a)=1 which is circular; (3) develop a new transference principle that works for arbitrary level sets, not just neighborhoods of 1.
directions.title: Monochromatic Pythagorean Triples in Every Level Set of Completely Multiplicative Functions

directions.description: For finite simple graphs G and H on disjoint vertex sets, the matching number of their join G∗H satisfies ν(G∗H) = min(ν(G) + |V(H)|, ν(H) + |V(G)|, ⌊(|V(G)| + |V(H)|)/2⌋). This is the foundational combinatorial theorem of the paper, proved via the Tutte-Berge formula, and underpins all subsequent results on squarefree powers of edge ideals of wheel, fan, and friendship graphs.
domain_bridges: extremal graph theory → commutative algebra of monomial ideals
directions.lean_theorem_stub: theorem matching_number_join {V W : Type*} [Fintype V] [Fintype W] [DecidableEq V] [DecidableEq W] (G : SimpleGraph V) (H : SimpleGraph W) : let join := G.join H; join.matchingNumber = min (G.matchingNumber + Fintype.card W) (min (H.matchingNumber + Fintype.card V) ((Fintype.card V + Fintype.card W) / 2)) :=
directions.proof_strategy: Instantiate the Tutte-Berge formula ν(X) = (|V(X)| - max_{S⊆V(X)}(o(X-S) - |S|))/2 for the join graph X = G∗H. Classify subsets S ⊆ V(G∗H) by their intersections S_G = S ∩ V(G) and S_H = S ∩ V(H). The key observation is that every vertex of V(H) not in S is adjacent to every vertex of V(G) not in S_G, so odd components of (G∗H) - S arise only from odd components of G - S_G together with the complete bipartite structure of the join. Derive that o(G∗H - S) = o(G - S_G) + o(H - S_H) when both S_G and S_H are nonempty, with boundary cases when one side is empty. Optimize over all S to obtain the min-expression.
directions.title: Matching Number of Arbitrary Graph Joins

directions.description: For a p-adic field F and a generic representation π of GL_r(F), the exterior square ε-factor defined via the Jacquet–Shalika local functional equation coincides with the exterior square ε-factor defined via the Langlands–Shahidi method: ε^{JS}(π, ∧², ψ) = ε^{Sh}(π, ∧², ψ). This is the main theorem (Theorem 1.1) of the paper. Formalizing it requires developing the theories of generic representations of GL_r over p-adic fields, both integral-representation (Jacquet–Shalika) and Langlands–Shahidi constructions of L- and ε-factors, and the local functional equation for the Jacquet–Shalika exterior square integrals.

    {F : Type*} [Field F] [IsPAdicField F]
    {r : ℕ} (π : GenericRepresentation (GL (Fin r) F))
    (ψ : AdditiveChar F ℂ) :
    epsilonFactorJS π (exteriorSquare r) ψ =
    epsilonFactorSh π (exteriorSquare r) ψ := by
  sorry
directions.proof_strategy: The original proof uses global methods: (1) construct a global automorphic representation whose local component at a designated p-adic place v is the given π, (2) exploit the equality of global ε-factors computed via both methods (using the global functional equation and the theory of global integrals), and (3) deduce the local equality by comparing local factors at all places, invoking the archimedean result of Jiang–Liu–Sun–Tian and the known equality ε^{Sh} = ε^{Gal} from Cogdell–Shahidi–Tsai. A formalization would need to first develop the local theories (Jacquet–Shalika integrals, Langlands–Shahidi L-functions, local ε-factors) and then formalize the globalization argument.
directions.title: Equality of Jacquet–Shalika and Langlands–Shahidi exterior square ε-factors for GL_n over p-adic fields

directions.description: For a cocompact Fuchsian group Γ with signature (g; m₁, …, mₛ) where g ≥ 2 (allowing elliptic elements, so the quotient H/Γ is a hyperbolic orbifold rather than a surface), a Γ-gain graph (G, ψ) is Γ-isostatic in the hyperbolic plane H if and only if it satisfies the (2, 3, 1+s, 0)-gain tightness condition. This extends the paper's main theorem from surface groups (s=0, yielding (2,3,1,0)-gain tightness) to general cocompact Fuchsian groups, predicting that each elliptic generator shifts the sparsity parameter by one.

    {Γ : Type*} [Group Γ] [CocompactFuchsian Γ]

    {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : GainGraph V Γ) :
    G.IsIsostaticInHyperbolicPlane ↔ G.IsGainTight 2 3 (1 + σ.numElliptic) 0 := by
  sorry
directions.proof_strategy: Extend the orbit rigidity matrix construction to Fuchsian groups with elliptic elements. Analyze how elliptic fixed points in the fundamental domain modify the dimension count for symmetry-preserving infinitesimal motions—each elliptic generator of order mᵢ should contribute an additional constraint at the corresponding cone point of the orbifold, shifting the effective sparsity parameter from 1 to 1+s. Verify the matroidal exchange axiom for the modified (2,3,1+s,0)-gain tight gain graphs, then prove the rank of the orbit rigidity matrix equals the rank of the gain sparsity matroid via an inductive Henneberg-type construction.
directions.title: Orbifold Rigidity Characterization for Fuchsian Groups with Torsion

directions.description: For a stable range dual pair (G', G) with G the smaller compact member (excluding (O_{2n,2n}, Sp_{2n})), every irreducible unitary representation π of G has a nonzero theta lift θ(π) that is also an irreducible unitary representation of G'. This is the compact-group specialization of Li's theorem (Theorem 2.2 in the paper), where the convergence and non-negativity of the Li form (Eq. 2) are automatic, yielding a clean statement: the full unitary dual of G embeds into the unitary dual of G' via theta correspondence.

    (not_exceptional : ¬IsExceptionalPair G' G)

    Nonempty (IrreducibleUnitaryRep G') ∧

      IsIrreducible θ_π ∧ IsUnitary θ_π := by

directions.title: Stable range theta lift preserves unitarity for compact smaller groups

directions.description: For any natural numbers n, l, r such that n >= (l+1)*r + l, there exists an interval packing of maximum possible size (n choose l) in the Boolean lattice restricted to levels l through l+r. This can be formulated as the existence of a function f mapping each l-sized subset T of [n] to an r-sized subset C_T disjoint from T, such that for any distinct l-sized subsets T1, T2, T1 is not contained in T2 union C_T2 and T2 is not contained in T1 union C_T1.

    ∃ (f : {T : Finset (Fin n) // T.card = l} → Finset (Fin n)),
      (∀ T, (f T).card = r ∧ Disjoint (T : Finset (Fin n)) (f T)) ∧
      (∀ T T', T ≠ T' → ¬((T : Finset (Fin n)) ⊆ T' ∪ f T') ∧ ¬(T' ⊆ T ∪ f T)) :=
  by sorry

Subsequently, prove that the resulting intervals [T, T ∪ C_T] are pairwise disjoint by showing that for any two distinct l-sets T1, T2, neither T1 ⊆ T2 ∪ C_{T2} nor T2 ⊆ T1 ∪ C_{T1} holds.
directions.title: Engel's Interval Packing Theorem

directions.description: For any field K with char(K) ≠ 2 and quadratic polynomials v, w ∈ K[x], the classical Wronskian v'w - vw' is exactly equal to the derivative-free Remainder-Polynomial Route (RPR) formulation. Specifically, v'w - vw' = 2x · Sres₁(v, w) + (v₁w - w₁v), where Sres₁(v,w) = v₂w - w₂v is the first subresultant of v and w, and vᵢ, wᵢ are the coefficients of xⁱ in v, w respectively. This identity generalizes symmetrically to the full Richelot triple (U, V, W), proving that RPR yields identical codomain polynomials not merely up to scalar units, but as an exact polynomial equality.
directions.lean_theorem_stub:
import Mathlib.Algebra.Polynomial.Basic
import Mathlib.Algebra.Polynomial.Derivative

variable {K : Type*} [Field K] (v w : K[X])

theorem rpr_exact_identity (hchar : (2 : K) ≠ 0) (hv : v.natDegree ≤ 2) (hw : w.natDegree ≤ 2) :
    Polynomial.deriv v * w - v * Polynomial.deriv w =
    2 * (Polynomial.X : K[X]) * (v.coeff 2 • w - w.coeff 2 • v) +
    (v.coeff 1 • w - w.coeff 1 • v) := by
  sorry
directions.proof_strategy: Expand both sides of the identity v'w - vw' = 2x(v₂w - w₂v) + (v₁w - w₁v) using the standard definition of the formal derivative v' = 2v₂x + v₁. Distributing the terms on the right-hand side and collecting coefficients of x², x, and 1 directly yields the expanded left-hand side, (v₂w₁ - v₁w₂)x² + 2(v₂w₀ - v₀w₂)x + (v₁w₀ - v₀w₁), proving the exact polynomial equality purely through algebraic manipulation without relying on scalar units or characteristic restrictions beyond char(K) ≠ 2.
directions.title: Exact Identity of Wronskian and Subresultant Richelot Formulations

directions.description: For any generalized star configuration ideal I of height h defined by n ≥ h+1 forms f₁,…,fₙ in a polynomial ring over a field, where any h of the forms constitute a regular sequence, the standard Veronese degree svd(I) equals lcm(1, 2, …, h). This extends the paper's main theorem for monomial star configurations to the generalized setting, predicting that the Veronese degree depends only on h, not on the specific choice of forms or the ambient polynomial ring.

    (I : Ideal (Polynomial k))

    svd I = Finset.lcm (Finset.Icc 1 h) id :=

Then extend to generalized star configurations by showing the Diophantine structure governing symbolic powers is invariant under regular sequences of forms—potentially via initial ideal arguments preserving svd, or by establishing that the symbolic Rees algebra of a generalized star configuration has the same Veronese structure as its monomial specialization.
directions.title: Standard Veronese Degree of Generalized Star Configurations Equals lcm(1,…,h)

directions.description: For any non-degenerate homogeneous quadratic form Q in 3 variables over ℤ whose zero set in ℙ²(ℚ) is nonempty, the dynamical system on [0,1] constructed by applying Romik's stereographic projection method to the Berggren tree of Q is ergodic and conservative with respect to its absolutely continuous invariant measure obtained via Keane's adaptation.

  sorry
directions.proof_strategy: For each quadratic form Q, construct the Romik-type map T_Q as a piecewise fractional linear transformation on [0,1] derived from the Berggren matrices. Show T_Q admits a Markov partition with the Gibbs-Markov property. Compute the invariant density using Keane's method (tracking how the quadratic form coefficients transform under the Berggren matrices). Apply the Hopf argument adapted to infinite measure spaces to establish ergodicity, and verify conservativity via the ratio ergodic theorem by checking integrability of the density against the return time function.
directions.title: Ergodicity of Dynamical Systems Induced from Berggren Trees

directions.description: For any simple graph G with n vertices and m edges, and for any 1 ≤ k ≤ n-1, the sum of the k largest Laplacian eigenvalues s_k(G) equals m + binom(k+1, 2) if and only if G is a threshold graph with clique number k+1.

    (n m k : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (h_m : G.edgeCount = m) (h_k : 0 < k ∧ k < n) :
    sum_k_largest_laplacian_eigenvalues G k = m + (k + 1) * k / 2 ↔
    IsThresholdGraph G ∧ CliqueNumber G = k + 1 := by sorry
directions.proof_strategy: Reduce the problem to the Grone-Merris-Bai theorem, which states s_k(G) ≤ ∑_{i=1}^k d_i^*(G) where d* is the conjugate degree sequence. Show that equality in Brouwer's bound implies equality in Grone-Merris-Bai, forcing the degree sequence to match the Laplacian eigenvalue sequence. Use the characterization of threshold graphs via their degree sequences and the specific sum m + binom(k+1, 2) to conclude that G must be a threshold graph with clique number k+1.
directions.title: Full Brouwer's Laplacian Conjecture Equality Characterization

directions.description: Every non-trivial 2-(v,k,λ) design admitting a flag-transitive automorphism group with socle PSL(2,q) (where q = p^f ≥ 4) that acts point-imprimitively on the design must satisfy v ∈ {15, 36, 85}, corresponding to exactly three isomorphism classes: the complementary design of PG(3,2), the complementary design of PG(3,4), and the Devillers–Praeger 2-(36,8,4) design. This captures the complete point-imprimitive classification proven in the paper and requires substantial design-theoretic and group-theoretic infrastructure to formalize.

    {q : ℕ} (hq : ∃ p f, q = p ^ f ∧ p.Prime ∧ f ≥ 1) (hq4 : q ≥ 4)
    {v k λ : ℕ} (D : TwoDesign v k λ) (hD : D.Nontrivial)
    (G : D.AutomorphismGroup) (hsoc : Socle G ≅ PSL2 q)
    (hft : G.FlagTransitive D) (himpr : G.PointImprimitive D) :
    v ∈ {15, 36, 85}
directions.proof_strategy: 1) Formalize 2-designs, automorphism groups, flag-transitivity, and point-imprimitivity in Lean. 2) Develop the subgroup structure of PSL(2,q) — specifically the classification of maximal subgroups (dihedral, parabolic, A4, S4, A5 subgroups). 3) Use the imprimitivity assumption to decompose the point set into blocks of imprimitivity, constraining v via the subgroup lattice. 4) Apply combinatorial parameter constraints (Fisher's inequality, divisibility relations r(k-1) = λ(v-1), bk = vr) together with the orbit-stabilizer theorem under PSL(2,q). 5) Case analysis on the possible systems of imprimitivity yields only v = 15, 36, 85.
directions.title: Point-Imprimitive 2-Designs with PSL(2,q) Socle Have Bounded Point Counts

directions.description: The number of lozenge tilings of the triangular region T_n equals the product over all 1 ≤ a < b ≤ 3n+2 with (a,b) ≠ (n+1,2n+2) of |1 + ζ^a + ζ^b|^(1/3), where ζ = exp(2πi/(3n+3)).

  (fun ab => Real.abs (1 + (zeta (3*n+3)) ab.1 + (zeta (3*n+3)) ab.2) ^ (1 / 3)) := by

Prove that the number of perfect matchings of G_n equals the absolute value of the determinant of M_n. Diagonalize M_n to compute its determinant, and verify that the resulting expression matches the given product formula.
directions.title: Exact Enumeration of Lozenge Tilings of Triangular Regions

directions.description: The maximum number of arcs in a loopless digraph on n vertices (allowing anti-parallel arcs) without a directed triangle is floor(n^2/2). This is the key combinatorial lemma (Theorem 1.1) from the paper, which bypasses the measure-theoretic difficulties of Bukh's original conjecture while capturing the core extremal insight.

    (r : α → α → Prop) [DecidableRel r]
    (h_no_loops : ∀ x, ¬ r x x)
    (h_no_dir_tri : ∀ x y z, r x y → r y z → r z x → False) :
    (∑ x, ∑ y, if r x y then (1 : ℕ) else 0) ≤ (Fintype.card α)^2 / 2 :=
  by sorry
directions.proof_strategy: Define the in-degree and out-degree of vertices. Prove that for any arc x -> y, the in-neighbors of x and out-neighbors of y are disjoint, hence in-deg(x) + out-deg(y) <= n. Sum over all arcs to get 2 * sum(d^+ * d^-) <= |E| * n. Apply Cauchy-Schwarz on the sum of total degrees squared to relate 4|E|^2 / n to 2|E|^2 / n + |E| n, and solve the quadratic inequality to conclude |E| <= n^2 / 2.
directions.title: Directed Mantel's Theorem for Loopless Digraphs

directions.description: For every integer n ≥ 3, there exists a constant c_n > 0 such that for every positive integer m, the density of primitive maximal binary forms of degree n (ordered by height) that simultaneously fail the integral Hasse principle for all F(x,y) = h with 1 ≤ h ≤ m is at least c_n / m^{n−2}. This refines the paper's result that this density is merely positive for each fixed m, conjecturing an explicit polynomial decay rate in m governed by the degree.

conjecture hasse_principle_failure_density {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≥ 3) :
  ∃ c : ℝ, c > 0 ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, m > 0 →
    let N := primitive_maximal_binary_forms_of_degree_and_height_le n m_
    let N_fail := forms_failing_integral_hasse_for_all_le n m_
    liminf (fun X => N_fail X m / N X) ≥ c / m ^ (n - 2)
directions.proof_strategy: Extend the Akhtari-Bhargava construction by tracking the m-dependence in the local solubility conditions and the Győry-type upper bounds on Thue inequality solutions. The key is to show that the proportion of forms excluded by each additional constraint h = k (for k ≤ m) shrinks as O(1/k^{n-1}), so the cumulative constraint for all h ≤ m leaves a proportion of order 1/m^{n-2}. This requires uniform estimates on the density of forms with prescribed local behavior at finitely many primes, combined with the sieving framework already present in the paper.
directions.title: Polynomial Decay of Simultaneous Hasse Principle Failure Density in Thue Equations

directions.description: For every number field K with ring of integers O_K, and every effective divisor D on the open unit disk 𝔻, there exists a holomorphic function f on 𝔻 whose Taylor coefficients all lie in O_K (viewed as a subring of ℂ via a fixed embedding σ : K ↪ ℂ) and whose zero divisor is exactly D. This directly generalizes the paper's Theorem 2.1 (the Gaussian-integer case O_K = ℤ[i]) to arbitrary rings of integers. The paper's proof for ℤ[i] exploits the Euclidean domain structure for an inductive rounding scheme; for general O_K, the full-rank lattice structure O_K ≅ ℤ^n should permit analogous nearest-lattice-point rounding within the jet-correction framework, but the non-uniqueness of rounding in non-Euclidean rings introduces subtleties that require new arguments.
domain_bridges: Complex analysis ↔ Algebraic number theory (holomorphic functions with algebraic integer coefficients)
Commutative algebra ↔ Complex analysis (divisor theory in restricted coefficient rings)
Diophantine approximation ↔ Complex analysis (lattice rounding in jet-correction schemes)
directions.lean_theorem_stub: theorem ring_of_integers_divisor_realization {K : Type*} [Field K] [NumberField K] (σ : K →+* ℂ) (D : EffectiveDivisor (Metric.ball (0 : ℂ) 1)) : ∃ (f : FormalPowerSeries ℂ) (h_conv : HasRadiusOfConvergence f 1) (h_holo : IsHolomorphicOn f (Metric.ball 0 1)) (h_coeffs : ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ (a : (𝓞 K)), f.coeff n = σ (a : K)), (zeroDivisor_of_holomorphic f h_holo) = D := by sorry
directions.proof_strategy: Adapt the paper's modified Weierstrass product with jet-correction operators. Step 1: Construct one-parameter deformations of Weierstrass elementary factors whose Taylor coefficients lie in O_K and which act as jet-correction operators preserving coefficients up to degree n while shifting the (n+1)-th coefficient by a controlled O_K-valued affine amount. Step 2: Since O_K ≅ ℤ^n as a ℤ-module, use nearest-lattice-point rounding (via the Minkowski theorem or LLL-type estimates) in place of the coordinate-wise rounding used for ℤ[i] ≅ ℤ². directions.description: Let adj be an irreflexive directed adjacency relation on n vertices (encoded as a predicate on Fin n × Fin n, with opposite arcs u→v and v→u both allowed). If the resulting digraph contains no directed triangle (no u→v→w→u), then the total number of arcs is at most ⌊n²/2⌋. This is the key combinatorial ingredient used in the paper to bound the measure of spherical sets avoiding x+y+z=0 via a probabilistic argument over SO(d), and it generalizes Mantel's theorem to directed graphs.

directions.proof_strategy: Adapt the appendix proof: show there exists a vertex v with total degree t(v) ≤ n (even n) or t(v) ≤ n−1 (odd n), then induct on n by removing v and applying the inductive hypothesis to the remaining digraph. The degree bound follows from the observation that for any arc x→y, the in-neighborhood of x and out-neighborhood of y are disjoint (else a directed triangle exists).
directions.title: Extremal arc count in digraphs without directed triangles (Brown–Harary theorem)

directions.description: For every finite tree T (viewed as a metric space with the shortest-path distance), the microscopic weighting assigns strictly positive weight to every vertex. The paper establishes that finite trees are of strictly negative type and hence admit a microscopic weighting, and that this weighting emphasizes boundary points and distributes mass widely. The open question is whether all vertex weights are necessarily positive — i.e., whether the signed measure is in fact a positive measure for trees. A counterexample would reveal a tree whose interior vertices receive negative microscopic weight, while a proof would show that the 'mass redistribution' from boundary emphasis never forces interior weights below zero.

    (h_tree : IsTreeMetric d)
    (h_strict_neg : IsStrictlyNegativeType d)
    (w : V → ℝ) (h_w : IsMicroscopicWeighting d h_strict_neg w) :
    ∀ x : V, w x > 0 := by
  sorry
directions.proof_strategy: Exploit the energy minimization characterization: the microscopic weighting minimizes the energy integral E(w) = Σ w(x)w(y)d(x,y) over signed measures of total mass 1. For trees, the distance matrix has recursive structure amenable to leaf-removal induction. Show that any signed measure of mass 1 on a tree with a negative-weight vertex can be modified to decrease energy, contradicting optimality. Alternatively, use the Schoenberg embedding characterization: the microscopic weighting corresponds to the closest point to the origin in the affine hull of the embedded vertices, and for trees this convex hull might be shown to contain the origin's projection with all positive barycentric coordinates.
directions.title: Positivity of Microscopic Weighting on Finite Trees

directions.description: The infimum μ₂ over all infinite sequences of radial cuts of the ratio between the maximum and minimum portion (adjacent pair of slices) sizes equals 1+ρ, where ρ is the unique real root of ρ²+ρ³=1 in (0,1). The paper proves μ₂ ≤ 1+ρ ≈ 1.75488 and Korsky proved μ₂ ≥ 5/3 ≈ 1.66667, but the exact value remains open.

  sorry
where
  ρ : ℝ := Classical.choose (Real.exists_eq_iff_sqrt_eq.mpr ⟨by norm_num, by ring⟩) -- real root of ρ² + ρ³ = 1
  μ₂ : ℝ := sInf {r | ∀ (seq : InfiniteCutSequence),
    supr (portion_ratio seq) ≤ r}
directions.proof_strategy: The upper bound μ₂ ≤ 1+ρ follows from the paper's construction and Proposition 1 on cyclic factor avoidance. The lower bound μ₂ ≥ 1+ρ requires showing that no infinite sequence of cuts can achieve a ratio strictly less than 1+ρ. This likely requires analyzing the combinatorial constraints on infinite words over the alphabet {0,1,2,3} with ratios 1:ρ:ρ²:ρ³, proving that any such word avoiding equal adjacent letters must contain a portion with ratio at least (1+ρ)/(ρ²+ρ³) = 1+ρ. A potential approach uses the substitution system properties: the map sending 0↦23 (or 32), 1↦0, 2↦1, 3↦2 shows that any valid infinite sequence must eventually approximate the fixed point, forcing portions near the extremal ratio.
directions.title: Optimality of the cake-cutting constant μ₂

directions.description: For a complete multipartite graph G = K_{n_1,...,n_m} with n_1 ≤ ... ≤ n_m, the path-free complex PF_t(G) is vertex decomposable if and only if t ≥ 2n_{m-1} - 1. Equivalently, this is exactly the range where PF_t(G) is shellable and sequentially Cohen-Macaulay. For t ≤ 2n_{m-1} - 2, the complex fails to be sequentially Cohen-Macaulay.

    (G : SimpleGraph (Σ i : Fin m, Fin (ns i)))
    (hG : IsCompleteMultipartite G) (t : ℕ) :
    VertexDecomposable (pathFreeComplex t G) ↔ t ≥ 2 * ns (Fin.last m - 1) - 1 := by

directions.proof_strategy: Formalize simplicial complexes and vertex decomposability in Lean, then define PF_t(G) as the simplicial complex of vertex subsets with no induced P_t. Define complete multipartite graphs and their part-size ordering. The forward direction (t ≥ 2n_{m-1}-1 ⟹ vertex decomposable) requires formalizing the explicit structural decomposition of PF_t(G) as a union of join complexes with a size-truncation term, then proving each join component is vertex decomposable and that the union preserves this property. The reverse direction (t ≤ 2n_{m-1}-2 ⟹ not sequentially Cohen-Macaulay) requires constructing a specific non-Cohen-Macaulay witness face or showing the homology fails the sequential Cohen-Macaulay condition, potentially via a Mayer-Vietoris spectral sequence argument.
directions.title: Vertex decomposability threshold for path-free complexes of complete multipartite graphs

directions.description: The number of length-n quasinecklaces Q_k(n) is exactly k times the number of length-n necklaces N_k(n) for all k ≥ 2 and n ≥ 1.
directions.proof_strategy: Demonstrate that each necklace corresponds to exactly k quasinecklaces via rotational symmetry or quasinecklace construction rules.
directions.title: Proportionality of quasinecklaces to necklaces

directions.description: Every exceptional rational function of degree 5 over F_q, where char(F_q) ∉ {2, 5}, is Möbius-equivalent to exactly one of four families: (1) the monomial X^5 (cyclic monodromy, single branch point), (2) a Rédei function of degree 5 (cyclic monodromy, two branch points), (3) a Dickson polynomial D_5(X, a) for some a ∈ F_q^× (dihedral monodromy with an F_q-rational branch point), or (4) a specific non-polynomial rational function arising from a rational 5-isogeny of an elliptic curve (dihedral monodromy without F_q-rational branch point). The monodromy group structure (cyclic vs. dihedral) and branch point rationality completely determine the function type.
directions.lean_theorem_stub: theorem degree5_exceptional_classification {F : Type*} [Field F] [Fintype F] (hchar : ringChar F ≠ 2 ∧ ringChar F ≠ 5) {f : RationalFunction F} (hf : IsExceptional f) (hdeg : natDegree f = 5) : ∃ μ : MobiusTransform F, (μ • f = monomial 5 ∨ μ • f = redeiFunction 5 ∨ ∃ a : Fˣ, μ • f = dicksonPolynomial 5 a ∨ ∃ b : F, μ • f = isogenyRationalFunction 5 b)
directions.proof_strategy: Formalize the key definitions: exceptional rational functions (permuting P^1(F_{q^m}) for infinitely many m via the Fried–Schur–Saxon criterion), Möbius equivalence, and arithmetic/geometric monodromy groups as permutation groups on 5 elements. Case-split by geometric monodromy group: cyclic case uses classification of transitive cyclic subgroups of S_5 with Riemann–Hurwitz constraining ramification to yield monomials and Rédei functions; dihedral case analyzes inertia subgroups of D_5 within S_5 and branch point rationality to derive Dickson polynomials and the elliptic isogeny family. Key intermediate lemma: for degree 5, the Riemann–Hurwitz formula restricts the possible ramification configurations to finitely many cases for each monodromy type.
directions.title: Classification of Exceptional Rational Functions of Degree 5 over Finite Fields

directions.description: For every doubly regular tournament T on n vertices (where n ≡ 3 mod 4, n ≥ 3), the metric dimension β(T) ≤ 2⌈log₂ n⌉. This extends the paper's O(log n) bound proven for certain doubly regular team tournaments to the classical and well-studied family of doubly regular tournaments, which are regular tournaments with parameters (n, (n-1)/2, (n-3)/4). The conjecture posits an explicit constant of 2, making it directly falsifiable by computing metric dimensions of small doubly regular tournaments (n = 3, 7, 11, 19, ...) and checking against the bound.

  sorry
directions.proof_strategy: Adapt Babai's probabilistic method as used in the paper: for a doubly regular tournament T, randomly sample k = 2⌈log₂ n⌉ vertices as a resolving set candidate. Compute the probability that two distinct vertices u, v receive the same distance vector from the sampled set. Use the strong regularity properties of doubly regular tournaments—specifically that every pair of vertices has exactly (n-3)/4 common out-neighbours—to bound the collision probability per pair by 1/2^k. Apply a union bound over all n(n-1)/2 pairs, choosing k so that the union bound is < 1, yielding a resolving set of size at most 2⌈log₂ n⌉.
directions.title: Logarithmic metric dimension of doubly regular tournaments

directions.description: The paper proves that for $k \ge 3$ and sufficiently large $n$, the maximum size of a subset of the $n \times n$ grid with no $k+1$ collinear points is exactly $kn$. This conjecture posits that the condition 'sufficiently large $n$' can be relaxed to $n > k$, meaning $f_k(n) = kn$ holds for all $k \ge 3$ and $n > k$. This would unify the trivial case ($n \le k$, where $f_k(n) = n^2$) and the asymptotic regime.
